metadata.title: THE 4D TRANSDUCTIVE PROOF: THE 9-DEGREE QUADRANT  AND THE CLOSURE OF GLOBAL INVERTIBILITY IN THE  JACOBIAN CONJECTURE (n = 2)
metadata.description:
This work presents “The 4D Transductive Proof: The 9-Degree Quadrant and the Closure of Global Invertibility in the Jacobian Conjecture (n = 2)”, a transductive formulation of the two-dimensional case of the Jacobian Conjecture.

The construction is based on a four-dimensional transductive geometry organized through the 9-degree Quadrant, the UNO Architecture, the Transductive Funnel, and the principle of closure of global invertibility. The starting point is a polynomial mapping F: C² → C² with constant and nonzero Jacobian determinant. From this initial condition, the formulation establishes a structural sequence connecting local conservation, geometric orientation, temporal torsion, transductive stability, global injectivity, and polynomial representation of the resulting state.

The 9-degree Quadrant is introduced as a geometric orientation element, with the structural coefficient

μ₀ = η sin(9°).

The transductive formulation relates the Jacobian field to the global evolution of the mapping through the four-dimensional algebraic structure. The resulting construction establishes a geometric mechanism in which the 9-degree orientation produces a repulsive separation between states and contributes to the closure condition associated with global invertibility.

The Transductive Funnel is then used to formulate the transition from the continuous or formal inverse representation to a defined polynomial state. The construction introduces the energy inequality

∑_{k=K}^{∞} ∥c_k∥² · e^{μ₀k} ≤ Limit E,

from which the transductive closure condition yields

c_k = 0 ∀ k > K.

Consequently, the inverse state is represented by the finite polynomial

G(y) = ∑_{k=0}^{K} c_k y^k.

The central closure condition is expressed as

IR(F) = 1,

which is associated in the formulation with global injectivity and the completion of the inverse structure.

The work therefore organizes the n = 2 case of the Jacobian Conjecture as a sequence of structural transformations:

Jacobian constant → Local Conservation → 9° Torsion (Time) → IR(F) = 1 → Global Injectivity → Transductive Funnel → G(y) ∈ C[y] → Defined State (Polynomial).

The final formulation, designated the Master Theorem of the Transductive Jacobian Conjecture (4D), integrates the differential, geometric, temporal, topological, and algebraic components into a single transductive architecture. The document also relates the construction to the UNO Architecture, the Transductive Funnel, the defined-state principle, and the broader geometric and transductive framework developed in the author's related research.

The work includes formal definitions, theorems, equations, derivations, the transductive closure construction, a glossary of technical terms, and a bibliography of references concerning the Jacobian Conjecture, polynomial automorphisms, inverse mappings, and related mathematical structures.

Keywords: JACOBIAN CONJECTURE; DIMENSION 2; 4D TRANSDUCTIVE PROOF; 9-DEGREE QUADRANT; TRANSDUCTIVE FUNNEL; UNO ARCHITECTURE; CONSTANT JACOBIAN; GLOBAL INVERTIBILITY; GLOBAL INJECTIVITY; TEMPORAL TORSION; LOCAL CONSERVATION; POLYNOMIAL STRUCTURE; POLYNOMIAL MAPPING; TRANSDUCTIVE GEOMETRY.
